cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Keep Hope Operational
cards.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my hands on the case like you. Warming up. Your visitor from tomorrow said hello; let's get their chair ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm stopping the loose lid falling off. The calculation says nobody can come through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Case secured. We did hear a reply. Test the microphone so your visitor can hear you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've put the microphone on the final probability. What does that number say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it there. Ask if they can hear you; I'll have their chair ready.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 imitates hands on a case as warming up; A3 covers B2's mundane repair while using heard contact to sustain B's visitor hope; A5 withholds the final number and assigns the next contact attempt.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's failed-arrival calculation prompts A3 to distinguish an actual reply; B4 discovers the covered probability and A5 deliberately redirects to a test.

relationship.evidence: B2 is invested enough to calculate arrival and B4 wants the figure; A3 offers B a useful contact role rather than merely commanding optimism.

heightening.evidence: A5 keeps the adverse figure covered precisely when B4 requests it, while preparing the already established visitor's chair.

specificity.evidence: A1 now names a visitor from tomorrow who said hello; partial voice contact is concrete evidence, unlike a device merely saying a date.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's short cover preserves face; A5's practical mic request and chair preparation show hope without an explanation of its psychology.
